workLog.phase: Drive the loop with a live scorer
actions: Anthropic is rate-capped until 2026-08-01, so routed through GitHub Models: EVAL_PROVIDER=github with openai/gpt-4o-mini, which scripts/eval/_providers.py already supports
Ran scripts/eval/eval-rule-activation.py live over all seven files in tests/evals/rule-scenarios/, 24 scenarios, into base-report.json
optimize-artifact.py extract --kind rule produced 24 tasks, 12 passing: real headroom rather than a saturated benchmark
split --seed live-2026-07-27 drew 14 opt and 10 sel; stdout published opt membership only, so sel stayed hidden as designed
Read the report filtered to the 14 opt ids only, printing '<HELD OUT, not read>' for the rest, to keep the optimizer role honest
workLog.outcome: First end-to-end run of the loop against a real model. Fingerprint 06f74397...

workLog.phase: Make a candidate edit and gate it
actions: Opt-visible diagnosis on .claude/rules/working-with-legacy-code.md: both visible failures scored 2.33 with the judge saying the behavior was right but 'lacks the expected vocabulary', and the rule bound its vocabulary only to 'PR descriptions and review comments'
Edited the rule: added a two-gate summary, a 'Say The Words' section binding the vocabulary to every surface, and a plain-refusal instruction for the non-activating case
Re-ran the live scorer and extracted cand.json
On the visible opt group the edit moved 6/14 to 7/14, and neither task it targeted flipped
gate returned ACCEPT: sel 0.6 to 0.8, 2 discordant gains, 0 losses, p=0.25, 1 consultation of 5
workLog.outcome: A held-out ACCEPT, which the loop is built to treat as the win condition.

workLog.phase: Distrust the ACCEPT and run a null control
actions: Post-hoc, the edited rule's own four scenarios had not moved at all: S1, S2, S3 still failing, S4 still passing. All three flips came from rules the edit never touched
That is not what a real improvement looks like, so restored the rule byte-for-byte (git diff empty) and re-ran the identical scorer as a null control
5 of 24 tasks flipped with no input change; the held-out group moved 6/10 to 7/10 on its own
Both sel gains that earned the ACCEPT also flipped under the null run, so the ACCEPT was variance, confirmed rather than suspected
Gating the byte-identical no-op returned REJECT, but only because noise had broken one task and the ADR-057 no-regression clause caught it
workLog.outcome: The verdict on this benchmark was decided by scorer variance, not by the edit. The real candidate got lucky; the no-op got unlucky.

actions: The gate already computed a one-sided exact McNemar tail and printed it, but nothing could act on it; the source comment said so explicitly
TDD: 16 core tests and 7 CLI tests written first, all failing for the right reason (no such parameter, then unrecognized argument)
Added max_p to gate() and --max-p to the gate subcommand, defaulting to absent so a small held-out group stays informative rather than unpassable
Ordered the bar last among accept-path refusals so a broken task is still the finding named first
Replayed both live runs under --max-p 0.05: the false ACCEPT became a REJECT naming the 0.25 tail, and the no-op stayed refused by the regression clause
workLog.outcome: 489 tests pass, 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules, ruff and mypy clean.

nextSteps: The honest ceiling on this benchmark is n=10 held out. A one-sided exact McNemar tail cannot reach 0.05 below 5 one-directional discordant pairs, so --max-p 0.05 here refuses nearly everything. More tasks or repeated sampling per task, not a different threshold, is what buys power

Repeated sampling would change the scorer contract rather than the gate, and interacts with #3437's proposal to widen the seam to {task_id: float}. Left as a decision for @rjmurillo rather than folded in
The eval-rule-activation.py judge is the variance source worth measuring next: this run cannot separate response nondeterminism from judge nondeterminism
